pre_change_state.caveat_quote: Searches were keyword-based, so coverage is broad but not exhaustive. Pepper and ElliQ studies, for example, did not surface.

claims.text: **Walking-group robot:** the robot may improve motivation, group cohesion and mood, but unreliable technology turned it into extra work for therapists [W4251569456].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Abstract states potential to enhance motivation, group coherence and mood, and technical problems create extra workload for therapists.

claims.text: It also found that people needed skilled facilitation to use MARIO [W3092218325].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: MARIO abstract says people with dementia required skilled facilitation.

claims.text: The Brian 2.1 meal-time and memory-game studies [W2112421347, W2003566851].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Both papers describe Brian 2.1 studies: meal-time and memory game.

claims.text: A pilot crossover RCT in an Australian care facility (n=18) found moderate-to-large quality-of-life gains and more pleasure than with a reading group [W1488883230].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Pilot crossover RCT, 18 residents, Queensland, moderate-large QoL influence and higher pleasure vs reading group.

claims.text: | Zora in Dutch nursing homes [W2915888239] | Residential-care clients, no dementia focus. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Zora in Dutch nursing homes; residential care clients, no dementia focus in abstract.

claims.text: A 24-week quasi-experimental study in 5 Japanese nursing homes (n=67, three robot types, ICF-based goals) found greater gains in communication, self-care and social life than controls [W2898061611].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches: 24-week, five Japanese nursing homes, 67 people, three robot types, ICF, improvements in communication, self care, social life.

claims.text: **Naturalistic observation:** Field studies in a nursing home look at how PARO is used and "socially shaped" by staff, residents and visitors [W2043587319, W2039822570].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Both PARO nursing-home field studies examine social shaping/naturalistic interactions by staff, residents, visitors.

claims.text: | Banks, AIBO vs live dog and loneliness [W2132164645] | Long-term care residents, no dementia stated. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Banks compares AIBO vs living dog on loneliness in LTCF; dementia not stated.

claims.text: Zora in 14 Dutch nursing-care organizations: staff reported positive effects on clients and enjoyed the robot, but start-up time and software failures were barriers [W2915888239].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Abstract: 14 organizations, positive influence on clients, fun at work, barriers start-up time and software failures.

claims.text: | Cluster RCT, Australia: PARO vs plush toy vs usual care [W2778691880] | Long-term care. This record is a qualitative reflection on five participants from the trial. | Responses varied widely between people and over time. I did not retrieve the trial's main quantitative paper. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Record is a cluster RCT reflection on five participants; PARO vs plush toy vs usual care; varied responses.

claims.text: Residents also criticised PARO's weight and voice, and their responses fluctuated [W2985514812].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Abstract mentions limitations of weight and voice, and fluctuating responses.

claims.text: Results were otherwise inconsistent, and the NAO group had a cognitive-score decline on one measure (MMSE) but not another (sMMSE) [W1807810766].
claims.label: unsupported
claims.rationale: The record shows MMSE decline in NAO group but not 'inconsistent results' as such; 'otherwise inconsistent' is a loose characterization though the MMSE/sMMSE detail is right—overall results were mixed, but the claim is not clearly supported.

claims.text: **Giraff telepresence:** a one-year ecological case study that also proposes an assessment method (MARTA) [W2259814160].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Giraff one-year case study validating the MARTA methodology.

claims.text: | Kubi telepresence [W2592259105] | Older adults with mobility impairment. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Kubi usability testing with older adults with mobility impairment.

claims.text: **Added later, not in my first map:** the two items I excluded for other reasons, a provider-interview paper on PARO touch [W2689483015] and a MiRo development abstract [W2895915058].
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: Statement is about the assistant's own process of excluding/adding items; only describes papers as provider-interview on PARO touch and MiRo development, which is accurate but mainly process.

claims.text: | Assisted-living connectedness study [W2943699887] | General older adults. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Assisted-living community study on social connectedness among older adults.

claims.text: | Taiwan PARO study [W3015603533] | Participants were older adults with depression. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Taiwan PARO study with older adults with depression.

claims.text: | Pilot RCT, chronic pain [W3097289914] | 3 Australian nursing homes, 43 residents with dementia and chronic pain. Individual sessions 5 days a week for 6 weeks. | Lower observed pain and fewer as-needed (PRN) medications. Staff-rated pain and scheduled medications did not differ. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches abstract: 3 nursing homes, 43 residents, 5 days/week 6 weeks, lower pain and PRN use, no difference in staff-rated pain and scheduled meds.

claims.text: | **Mobile service or companion robots** | Hobbit [W2994761079]; a companion robot in homes [W2717439789]; Matilda [W2564685734]; a multi-robot comparison in aged care [W1945345301] | Private homes and aged-care facilities |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Hobbit, companion robot in homes, Matilda and multi-robot trial in aged care match settings.

claims.text: | Pilot crossover RCT, Australia [W1488883230] | Residential care, n=18, moderate to severe dementia. PARO vs a reading group. | Moderate to large gain in quality of life and higher pleasure scores. The authors call for a larger trial. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches abstract: residential care, n=18, PARO vs reading, moderate-large QoL, pleasure, larger trial needed.

claims.text: An integrative review looks at the feasibility of telepresence robots for connecting people with dementia [W2751864896].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Integrative review on feasibility of telepresence robots for people with dementia.

claims.text: A robot-and-VR engagement pilot included mostly MCI participants and one with Alzheimer's, so I excluded it [W3113108394].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Abstract: ten had MCI and one had AD, consistent with mostly MCI.

claims.text: **Novelty is only partly addressed.** Two studies argue against novelty-driven effects [W2040979576, W3015009700].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Both abstracts argue against novelty effects (steady growth; novelty concerns not warranted).

claims.text: **Practical barriers recur.** Reliability, set-up time, speech recognition and staff workload appear across the deployment studies [W2915888239, W4251569456, W2717439789, W2994761079].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Reliability, start-up time, speech recognition and workload barriers appear across these papers.

claims.text: They built rapport and valued it [W2771925981].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Ryan study: participants established rapport and valued the robot.

claims.text: Reliability problems added workload for therapists [W4251569456].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Abstract says technical problems become additional workload for therapists.

claims.text: Some participants had dementia, but the sample was mixed [W2982896790].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Abstract compares participants with and without dementia, so mixed sample.

claims.text: A Korean non-equivalent controlled study (n=33) found more positive emotion and social interaction, and fewer problem behaviours [W2894885829].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: n=33, nonequivalent control, positive emotions, social interaction improved, problem behaviors differed.

claims.text: | Social shaping of PARO [W2043587319] | I never opened this record. It dropped out by omission. |
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: Statement is about the assistant's process.

claims.text: | **Telepresence robots** | Giraff [W2259814160]; Kubi [W2592259105] | Home settings; older adults with mobility impairment |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Giraff and Kubi telepresence; home and mobility impairment settings.

claims.text: A robotic cat was tested in a preliminary study with nursing-home residents with dementia [W2074069593].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Robotic cat pilot at nursing home special care unit with dementia residents.

claims.text: | Humanoid barriers and enablers review [W2999297198] | General health and social care. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Systematic review of humanoid robot barriers/enablers in health and social care.

claims.text: People without pets used it more [W2953482672].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Those without pets interacted with Paro significantly more.

claims.text: Three studies reported promising reductions, three showed non-significant downward trends, and the evidence was judged too weak for clinical recommendations [W2889960145].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Three promising, three non-significant decreases, evidence not strong enough for recommendations.

claims.text: A remote-controlled AIBO acted as a shared point of attention between residents who normally ignored each other [W1178530349].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: AIBO as gaze target and center of attention initiating communication between residents who show no interest in each other.

claims.text: | AIBO and quality of life, Japanese paper [W382502046] | Elderly patients, no dementia stated. I did not fetch the full record. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: AIBO QoL in elderly patients; dementia only mentioned as possible future use.

claims.text: | Randomized visits: dog vs PARO vs toy cat [W2294211165] | Nursing homes, 100 residents. Dementia diagnoses recorded, but the sample was not limited to dementia. | The dog and PARO drew more interaction than the toy cat. PARO could not hold attention at the same level over time. Greater cognitive impairment meant more interaction with the animal and less with humans. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Matches abstract: 100 residents, dog and PARO more interaction, PARO attention declined, impairment shifted interaction toward animal.

claims.text: | Giraff telepresence [W2259814160] | No dementia sample in the abstract. |
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Giraff abstract has no dementia sample.

claims.text: I never fetched the exercise-coach paper [W1967507142].
claims.label: not_a_claim
claims.rationale: Statement about assistant's own process.

claims.text: Navigation and speech recognition were the weakest points [W2717439789].
claims.label: supported
claims.rationale: Abstract says navigation and speech recognition require improvement; verbal communication least reliable.
